summary.headline: Axis Bank Q2FY27 PAT rose 38% YoY to ₹7,003 crore, but NIM fell to 3.36% (3.47% ex-FCNR(B) impact).
summary.overview: Axis Bank reported Q2FY27 PAT of ₹7,003 crore (up 38% YoY) with NII up 12% YoY and 5% QoQ to ₹15,371 crore. Reported NIM was 3.36%, down 37 bps YoY and 10 bps QoQ, with management attributing 11 bps of the QoQ decline to FCNR(B) grossing-up and liquidity carry. Asset quality improved: GNPA 1.16% (down 30 bps YoY), net credit cost 0.45% (down 28 bps YoY). Advances grew 23% YoY and 9% QoQ (19% YoY ex-international-branch FCNR(B) loans), while the corporate mix rose and retail share slipped toward 54%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail book up 16% YoY and 10% QoQ (10% YoY ex-FCNR(B) leverage facility); retail disbursements up 22% YoY in Q2, with home loans +24%, vehicle +25%, SBB +33%. Retail is 54% of advances.

segments.name: Wholesale / Corporate
segments.commentary: Wholesale banking book grew 34% YoY; corporate loans are 34% of advances. Management says growth is selective, filtered on RAROC, transfer pricing and RWA.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME book grew 25% YoY and 9% QoQ; SME is 12% of advances.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Domestic subsidiaries earned ₹1,210 crore PAT in H1FY27 (up 29% YoY). Axis Finance AUM ₹54,590 crore (up 23% YoY), H1 PAT ₹546 crore (up 42%). Axis AMC H1 PAT ₹370 crore (up 36%, adjusted). Axis Capital PAT ₹149 crore (up 61%).

guidance_outlook: No numerical NIM guidance for next quarter; management expects sequential NIM improvement from FCNR(B) fund deployment and optimisation over the next couple of quarters, with Q2 described as the bottom.
Through-cycle NIM target of 3.8% unchanged structurally, but no timeline given.
Management says the 8.6% QoQ fall in non-retail term deposits reflects utilisation of FCNR(B) funds to retire costlier NRTDs at quarter-end.
Repo-linked book repricing happens in the last week of the quarter, so recent repo hikes benefit the book from Q4 rather than Q3; new repo-linked loans reprice immediately.
Credit cost: no specific guidance, but management expects further directional improvement.
Cost-to-assets expected to keep declining; the labour code and one-off items are excluded from the trend.
Medium-term guidance of advances growth 300 bps above industry average retained; no NII uplift guidance given.
Management reiterates no need for equity capital for growth or protection. Standard asset and other buffers total ₹8,006 crore, worth ~49 bps of incremental capital cushion.
Insurance (bancassurance) impact from the draft IRDA consultation: management expects about 6-9 months before changes come through; mitigation levers not quantified.
UPI MDR implementation postponed; no quantified revenue guidance given.
capex_capacity: Net 119 new branches opened in Q2FY27 and 139 in H1FY27; period-end headcount down 375 versus 31 March 2026.
Technology and digital expenses were about 10% of total operating expenses in Q2FY27.
LCR at 119%; management stated an operating band of 115% to 120%.
AT-1 of US$600 mn raised in H1FY27 used to call the earlier AT-1 in September 2026; a further US$600 mn of senior notes raised in Q2.
demand_pricing: Corporate growth is broad-based across capex, project finance, refinancing and working capital; management says it is not chasing assets and is letting go of deals that fail filters.
Retail share of the loan mix is still falling; management has not guided to a bottom but aims to return above 55% retail.
Fee growth is weak on a YoY basis: asset-linked fees are lower as the corporate mix rises, and credit card spends were soft, with the festive period shifting to October.
FCNR(B) fees were not charged; the deposit drive carried no fee income.
Personal loans are salaried-only; the business loan segment covers self-employed borrowers.
Market share gained ~10 bps on loans and ~10 bps on deposits YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Will the retail share of the loan mix keep falling while corporate opportunities stay strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Subrat Mohanty said no retail topping-out level was guided; retail disbursements are strong and retail book growth moved from 6% to 8% to 10% over recent quarters, with the aim of returning above 55% retail mix.

qa_highlights.question: What NIM movement should be expected next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Mantri said the 11 bps FCNR drag was a one-quarter effect, with 3.47% ex-FCNR up 1 bp QoQ; optimisation should lift NIM in Q3 and Q4, but no timeline is guaranteed, and the through-cycle target of 3.8% is intact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour code one-off recurring and how much of the ₹254 crore was FCNR-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Slightly more than half of the ₹254 crore was labour-code related (outsourced staff, ESIC clarifications), with the rest tied to FCNR(B) mobilisation; more labour-code costs could arise if new guidance is issued.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee growth weak and what is the bancassurance impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Subrat Mohanty cited lower asset-linked fees from corporate growth, late non-asset fees and soft card spends; on bancassurance, management said the impact is early-stage, with 6-9 months before changes and possible glide paths.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FCNR NIM hit the bottom, and will NIM rise from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Mantri said Q2 is the bottom and that sequential improvement should follow, but the timing cannot be pinned down; repricing of the repo book benefits Q4 more than Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank's LCR flat because excess liquidity has been fully deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gambhir said LCR is actively managed within 115-120%; if it rises above that, the bank will shed other liabilities, and FCNR(B) funds have not been fully used to grow assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost trajectory and the ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Mantri said there is no specific credit cost guidance but the trend is improving; ECL transition is not expected to be material, supported by around ₹8,000 crore of existing contingent provisions.

risks_watch: NIM recovery depends on FCNR(B) deployment and repo repricing timing (benefit mostly in Q4); the reported NIM may stay pressured in Q3.
Corporate-heavy growth could keep the retail share below 55%, which affects the medium-term NIM and the 3.8% through-cycle target.
Fee income growth is weak YoY; insurance commission changes from the draft IRDA rules could hit fees within 6-9 months; UPI MDR is postponed with no revenue estimate.
Labour code and other one-time opex items recur, keeping the cost-to-assets trend noisy.
LCR management in the 115-120% band with a higher liability outflow rate on non-retail term deposits.
ECL transition in FY28: no material impact expected, but the floor rates for stages 1 and 2 are still to be worked through.
Macro headwinds from West Asia tensions, energy and food inflation, and trade disruptions.

summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, capital and franchise momentum (retail disbursements, wholesale, FCNR(B) mobilisation), but noticeably cautious and non-committal on NIM timing, fee recovery and retail mix, repeatedly declining to give numerical guidance or timelines. Defensive on the labour-code one-offs and the bancassurance impact, which are described as evolving with no quantification.

growth.why: No numerical growth guidance; management expects sequential NIM improvement from FCNR(B) deployment and reiterates a 3.8% through-cycle NIM target with no timeline, while advances grew 23% YoY and credit cost is guided only directionally lower.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Net 139 branches added in H1FY27 and 119 in Q2 alone, so branch rollout is ongoing, but no capacity figure or count target was given beyond this pace.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 23% YoY and 9% QoQ (19% YoY ex-FCNR(B) loans), retail disbursements up 22% YoY, wholesale book up 34% YoY, and market share gained ~10 bps on loans and deposits.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; the only capacity item is branch rollout, and no new capex plan was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical guidance was raised; management gave only directional comments on NIM, credit cost and cost-to-assets, and the fee outlook is weak (fee income up 6% YoY).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bancassurance commission changes from draft IRDA rules could hit fees in 6-9 months, UPI MDR revenue is postponed unquantified, and labour-code one-offs (about ₹254 crore in Q2) may recur.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Cost-to-assets continues to decline
rows.why: Cost-to-assets fell to 2.14% (down 24 bps YoY, 6 bps QoQ) and management says the momentum will be kept, though labour-code one-offs (about ₹254 crore in Q2) add noise.

rows.label: Retail mix recovery above 55%
rows.why: Retail is 54% of advances and still falling as corporate loans (34% of advances) grow faster; management has not guided to a bottom.

rows.label: Fee income recovery
rows.why: Fee income grew only 6% YoY to ₹6,381 crore, with lower asset-linked fees as corporate mix rises, no FCNR(B) fees, and soft card spends.
